content.text: No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee exists anywhere in the document. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee on Customer, which matches the preferred position. Section 9.4 gives us convenience termination with fees owed only for conforming Services delivered plus a refund of prepaid Fees — no termination charge or acceleration; Section 27.3 likewise allows force-majeure termination "without penalty"; Section 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due; and Section 24.4 prevents Vendor from accelerating Fees on our change of control. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", acceleration and minimum-fee language return nothing payable by Customer. The take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 is the only penalty-like exposure, but it is a volume commitment addressed under the minimum-commitment rule and is not framed as liquidated damages, so we do not flag it twice here.
